After testing Ghostty for a while: input lag is higher than xfce4-terminal, font rendering is blurrier, UI is less consistent with my desktop, and it has three to four times the memory footprint. This is going to be an uninstall for me.
To blend Ghostty in better with XFCE, add to config: window-theme = system, gtk-titlebar = false, gtk-wide-tabs = false, gtk-adwaita = false.
Building from source needs specific deps: 'sudo apt install libgtk-4-dev libadwaita-1-dev git', otherwise you get 'unable to spawn glib-compile-resources' errors.
It also seems to need a fairly new gtk4. At least the version in Ubuntu 22.04 is too old.

Thanks for the minimum-contrast option (ghostty.org/docs/config/reference#minimum-contrast) - sick of tools with unreadable dark-on-black text. Look forward to never manually theming a terminal again!
selection-foreground and selection-background config to set highlight colors makes a massive difference, versus the translucent selection on Mac or defaults on Windows/Linux.
According to an 11-month-old benchmark, Ghostty had the worst input latency across all contenders; a newer benchmark from ~4 months ago shows avg 13ms, which feels about right now.
On throughput (catting a large file), Ghostty performs very well, among the same league as Alacritty and Ptyxis.
It feels amazing on linux. I find it very noticably better than konsole. Foot/Alacritty also feel amazing but they don't have some features of Ghostty.

Using its own TERM is a deliberate design decision that can cause SSH 'missing or unsuitable terminal' errors on servers that hardcode xterm as the standard; there's a terminfo fix documented but it's friction.

I have tried every possible setting but SSH ends up breaking more often than not. As opposed to iTerm which just works. Sometimes I'm back to seeing ESC codes when I press an arrow; quit & restart fixes it but it's friction.
The quick terminal feature is ghostty's killer feature for me.
Ghostty is awesome and I almost dropped iTerm for it until I hit cmd-f and nothing happened.
Missing search and weird ssh control character issues are my blockers. It's great otherwise!

Yeah I quickly (and unfortunately!) switched back to Warp, as Ghostty was a little too barebones for my use case. Word to the wise: Ghostty's default scrollback buffer is only ~10MB, but it can easily be changed with a config option.
Missing scrollbars. That and ctrl-f are my two annoyances, apart from that I love ghostty and use it daily at work.
I'm just waiting for them to implement drag-and-drop on KDE. Right now it only works on GNOME, and although Ghostty is great I'm not going to switch to GNOME just for a terminal emulator.

PROBE runtime (recorded 2026-09-04, Ghostty 1.3.1 via brew cask): `ghostty +list-actions` enumerates 85 bindable actions (new_split, new_tab, ...) and `ghostty +help` documents the +action CLI surface, but no remote-control/IPC interface was found — the macOS CLI supports config +actions only, so an external script or agent cannot send commands to or read output from a running Ghostty instance.
